investigation.scenes_py_timeline_reference: pipeline/stage_a/scenes.py detect_shots() runs `ffmpeg -i <video> -filter:v select='gt(scene,T)',showinfo` and parses pts_time fields (lines 42-80). Per stage-a.yml lines 448-452, `scenes all` is invoked on $ORIGINAL_PATH = jobs/<id>/ingest.json's original_path = work/original.<ext> (the ingested source, NOT a re-encoded copy — bug-68 removed the 720p analysis copy entirely; bundle.py lines 18/186 confirm analysis_720p.mp4 is no longer produced). pts_time values are the ORIGINAL source container's own presentation timestamps, zero-based from source start. Baseline composites extract_baseline_composites() (lines 519-566) also run on the same original: fps=1,tile=3x2 -> grid_NNNNN.jpg renamed to frame_<seq*6>.jpg, so frame_000042.jpg = source seconds [42,48). Event composites emit_event_composite() seek with input-side `-ss <center-2> -t 4 -i <original>` (lines 380-404), same reference. CONCLUSION: scenes/screenshot timeline = original source video timeline, zero offset, no resample/trim between.
investigation.transcript_timeline_reference: stage-a.yml lines 434-438: `ffmpeg -y -i $ORIGINAL_PATH -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le work/audio.wav` then transcribe work/audio.wav. Same $ORIGINAL_PATH as scenes. The -vn/-ac/-ar re-encode extracts audio starting at source t=0 with no seek/trim, so the WAV is 1:1 time-locked to the source. faster-whisper transcribe() (transcribe.py lines 188-197) returns segment start/end on that WAV's timeline = original source timeline. transcribe_to_json persists audio_duration_seconds = last segment end (lines 260,280). CONCLUSION: transcript timeline = original source timeline, SAME reference as scenes.py. No offset between them.
investigation.renderpy_extraction_reference: pipeline/stage_b/render.py produce_merged_video() line 309: for each cut emits `-ss {start_seconds:.3f} -to {end_seconds:.3f} -i <src>` where src=original_video (the same ingested source re-obtained by Stage B). Input-side seek against the ORIGINAL source timeline. render_merged() line 617 probes src_duration = common.probe_duration_seconds(original_video) (ffprobe format=duration). Lines 663-676 validate each reconciled cut range against [0, src_duration+0.5]. setpts stretch (line 327) only retimes, never moves boundaries. CONCLUSION: render extraction timeline = original source timeline, SAME reference. The three producers/consumers (scenes, transcript, render) all agree on the original source timeline.
investigation.automatic_py_offset_check: pipeline/plan/automatic.py: the model reads transcript.json, scene_index.json, key_moments.json via tools and opens screenshot composites. composite_window_seconds() (lines 238-251) maps frame_NNNNNN.jpg -> [N, N+window) and event_MMMMMMMMM.jpg -> [center-2, center+2] using the SAME zero-based source-time the filenames encode (matches scenes.py naming). visual_grounding_errors() (lines 649-682) requires each cut's start/end to be covered by opened composite windows, enforcing that chosen seconds correspond to visually-confirmed source moments. No additive/subtractive offset is applied anywhere to start_seconds/end_seconds in automatic.py; seconds are taken verbatim from the evidence. CONCLUSION: no systematic offset in automatic.py's mapping. (Residual: it trusts the model's transcription of seconds, but the visual-grounding check bounds that error to one composite window ~6s, and there is no CODE-level systematic offset.)
investigation.additional_findings: CRITICAL GAP (candidate 5 CONFIRMED as a real defect): production.json carries video_duration_seconds (an integer) that Stage A's prompt.py line 1135 embeds from the probed source duration and the model echoes back. pipeline/plan/schema.py validate_production_plan() uses it ONLY to check cuts' end_seconds <= video_duration_seconds (lines 238-239). Stage B render_merged() probes the ACTUAL src_duration via ffprobe (line 617) and validates cut ranges against THAT (lines 663-676), but NOWHERE compares the plan's DECLARED video_duration_seconds against the PROBED src_duration. If the two diverge (stale plan, wrong/older source re-fetched via bug-69 refetch_source.py, source edited/replaced between Stage A and Stage B, or a hallucinated/wrong duration in a manual plan), every start_seconds/end_seconds is interpreted against a DIFFERENT-length timeline than the planner used — so a cut can land on entirely the wrong scene while still passing both validators (each cut end <= declared duration AND <= actual duration). This is exactly the operator's symptom: internally-consistent numbers pointing at the wrong actual moment. For the reported job manual-1788116412985 the declared 9283s is internally consistent (cuts 7028-8162 within it, single-file torrent 2908144950 bytes matches ingest.json size so Stage A and Stage B used the same MKV), so the bug is LATENT/structural rather than proven for that one file — but the missing declared-vs-actual guard is the concrete, fixable defect that lets the symptom occur silently.
